assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave researchers a powerful framework for understanding strongly correlated electrons and has become central to modern condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Georges, Vollhardt, and Kotliar are leading architects of the method and its influential applications; the broader development involved a substantial research community.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been used and developed for decades, with extensive theoretical and computational validation.
uncertainties: The long-term reach of the method is clear, but dividing credit among its originators and subsequent developers is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed a tunable route to correlated and superconducting states, opening a major new direction in quantum-materials research.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald established the theoretical mechanism for flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group demonstrated the striking correlated behavior experimentally.
assessment.maturity: The phenomenon has been intensively reproduced and extended across moiré systems, though the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: The microscopic origins and relation among the different observed phases remain under active study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic crystals established control of light through periodic structures, enabling important advances in optical physics and device design.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch and John independently developed the central concept, while Joannopoulos made major contributions to its theoretical understanding and development.
assessment.maturity: The underlying physics is well established and has supported decades of research and practical photonic applications.
uncertainties: The independent origins and broad community contributions make a three-person attribution challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measurements of fractional charge and anyonic statistics in quantum Hall systems probe foundational properties of topological matter and fractionalization.
assessment.attribution: These researchers made important experimental contributions to detecting and characterizing fractionalized excitations; the underlying quantum Hall discoveries and many experiments involved others.
assessment.maturity: Fractional charge is well supported, while experimental claims about statistics have advanced through increasingly precise but technically demanding measurements.
uncertainties: The case depends on which measurements are considered decisive for demonstrating statistics and how credit is allocated across experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a two-dimensional electron gas at oxide interfaces showed that interfaces can host electronic states and behaviors absent in the bulk materials.
assessment.attribution: Ohtomo and Hwang reported the landmark interface result; Mannhart helped establish and develop the broader field of oxide heterostructures.
assessment.maturity: The result motivated extensive experimental and theoretical work, although individual interface phases and proposed mechanisms vary in robustness.
uncertainties: The breadth of phenomena grouped under oxide interfaces makes it hard to define one discovery and its boundaries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are stable, topologically structured spin textures that have reshaped research in magnetism and opened promising routes for spin-based devices.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer, Wiesendanger, and Tokura made major contributions to observing, imaging, and developing skyrmion physics in distinct material settings.
assessment.maturity: Skyrmions are firmly established in several systems, while reliable device use and some proposed dynamical advantages remain under development.
uncertainties: The discovery and development span theory, materials, and imaging, with significant contributions beyond these three researchers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic-resolution qPlus force microscopy made it possible to probe local forces and resolve chemical structure at surfaces with exceptional precision.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor approach, and Meyer and Gross contributed substantially to its refinement and landmark applications.
assessment.maturity: The technique is well established and has enabled many reproducible measurements in surface science.
uncertainties: The case is stronger as a major enabling instrument than as a single fundamental discovery, and instrument development has broad contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices created a clean, controllable platform for simulating quantum many-body systems and observing phenomena that are difficult to access in solids.
assessment.attribution: Bloch and Greiner led landmark experiments, while Zoller provided foundational theory for quantum simulation with trapped atoms.
assessment.maturity: The platform has been validated across many experiments and continues to produce new results; some applications as a quantitative simulator are still developing.
uncertainties: The field has many important experimental and theoretical contributors, and its eventual impact on understanding real materials is not yet settled.
